Subject: Request: pricing reopener & SOW consolidation for Order Form #3149

Hi Laura —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We reviewed the proposed Order Form (#3149) with our finance and legal teams overnight. Two items came up that are high priority for us to close the deal this month: 1) a narrow "pricing reopener" tied to cloud-cost indices for year 2, and 2) consolidating two small implementation SOW exhibits into a single Exhibit A to simplify procurement.

Can you confirm whether Redwood is open to including a limited reopener (cap on increases, 60-day notice, mutual audit right) and whether the SOW consolidation can be handled as a single change order rather than a full MSA amendment? Our procurement lead (Tom) is keen to avoid multiple signature flows.

Attaching the procurement checklist for your reference.

Best,
Samira
Samira Khan
Sr. Procurement Manager, Medicomp

Hi Samira —

Appreciate the clear ask. Short answer: yes, we can do a limited pricing reopener and we can consolidate the two implementation exhibits into a single Exhibit A via change order — both are reasonable. A couple quick notes so we align on scope: 1) reopener language should include a max% increase (we typically cap at 8% for index-linked adjustments or provide a fixed floor/ceiling), 2) consolidation of SOWs will require a single updated Exhibit A that preserves acceptance criteria and milestones.

I've attached an initial draft Order Form with proposed reopener bullets and a consolidated Exhibit A for your review. Karthik (commercial) and Monica (legal) are on copy to confirm final wording.

Proposed next steps:
- You review the attached draft and tell us whether the 8% cap is acceptable (or propose a cap you need).
- If okay, Monica will produce a short change order template to avoid full MSA amendment.
- Tech sync/acceptance scoping call w/ implementation if any milestone language needs tuning.

Can we target a 9/3 signature window? Happy to align on an internal exec approval if needed.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Director, Sales (Enterprise) 
Redwood Inference

Laura / Monica —

Adding a couple of commercial preferences inline:
- We prefer a 0-8% annual cap but are open to banded adjustments tied to a third-party index (e.g., cloud CPI or infra-cost index).
- Any reopener should be mutual (both parties can trigger) with a 60-day notice and a mandatory mediation step prior to unilateral changes.
- For SOW consolidation: keep the implementation acceptance tests verbatim; do not merge the milestone payments unless Medicomp agrees to the new schedule.

If legal can give quick sign-off on the change order flow (instead of an MSA amendment), it will shave 2-3 weeks off procurement.

-karthik
Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

Laura / Karthik —

Thanks for the context and the draft. High level: we can avoid a full MSA amendment in this case and handle the changes via a single change order + updated Exhibit A, provided we do two things:

1) Preserve all cross-references to the MSA (indemnity, data protection, liability caps) in the consolidated Exhibit A and add an acknowledgement line so the procurement team can't argue that consolidation rewrites substantive MSA protections.

2) Reopener language (suggested):
"Either party may, not more than once in any 12-month period after the Effective Date, request in writing an adjustment to the pricing set forth in the Order Form based on documented material changes in third-party infrastructure costs. Any proposed adjustment shall include supporting calculations and be subject to a maximum annual increase of 8%. The parties shall engage in good faith negotiation for no fewer than sixty (60) days. If the parties are unable to agree during such period, the dispute resolution process in Section X of the MSA shall apply, and no unilateral price increase shall take effect prior to resolution."

3) Implementation milestones: we will keep milestone payments separate unless Medicomp confirms agreement in writing to the merged schedule.

I attached a marked-up MSA_redline_v3.docx with the reopener clause inserted and a short change-order template (MSA_ChangeOrder_Template.docx) you can use. Also included a one-page summary for procurement that explains why this is a change order (not an amendment).

I can be on the call with Medicomp legal if they want to walk through the language.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Senior Counsel, Contracts 
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MSA_redline_v3_comments.docx]
